extracted.intended_audience: issuers, registrants, underwriters, and their counsel preparing SEC registration statements and prospectuses (Regulation S-K filers)
extracted.subtask_description: Requirements and disclosure standards for information to be included in SEC registration statements and prospectuses (items in Regulation S-K), including cover pages, prospectus summary, use of proceeds, plan of distribution, insider trading arrangements, and related undertakings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Item 408 — Insider trading arrangements and policies
rubrics_metrics.description: Disclose whether, during the registrant's last fiscal quarter (or fourth fiscal quarter for annual reports), any director or officer adopted or terminated: (i) any contract, instruction or written plan intended to satisfy the affirmative defense conditions of Rule 10b5-1(c) (a “Rule 10b5-1 trading arrangement”); and/or (ii) any “non-Rule 10b5-1 trading arrangement.” Identify whether the trading arrangement is intended to satisfy the affirmative defense of Rule 10b5-1(c), and provide a description of the material terms (other than price terms) such as name and title of the director/officer, date adopted/terminated, duration, aggregate number of securities to be purchased/sold.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The disclosure required by paragraphs (a)(1) and (2) must be provided in an Interactive Data File as required by 17 CFR 232.405 per the EDGAR Filer Manual. Disclose whether the registrant has adopted insider trading policies reasonably designed to promote compliance with insider trading laws/rules and listing standards; if not adopted, explain why. If adopted, file such policies and procedures as an exhibit (inclusion of such policies in the code of ethics and filing of the code satisfies the exhibit requirement). For Item 408, a “non-Rule 10b5-1 trading arrangement” is defined where the covered person asserts adoption while not aware of material nonpublic information and the arrangement either (i) specified amount/price/date; (ii) included written formula/algorithm/computer program to determine trades; or (iii) did not permit subsequent influence by the covered person (and any person exercising influence was not aware of material nonpublic information).

rubrics_metrics.name: Item 501 — Forepart of Registration Statement and Outside Front Cover Page of Prospectus
rubrics_metrics.description: The registrant must furnish specified information in plain English on the front cover page of the registration statement and on the outside front cover page of the prospectus (outside cover limited to one page). If applicable, disclose specified items on the outside cover page including: (1) Name (foreign registrant must give English translation); (2) Title and amount of securities offered and brief description; (3) Offering price information and how presented; (4) Market(s) and trading symbol(s); (5) Cross-reference to risk factors and page number; (6) State legend; (7) Commission legend; (8) Underwriting information/arrangements; (9) Date of prospectus; (10) Prospectus “Subject to Completion” legend and language.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Instructions include: avoid confusion if name matches another company or implies a different business; state separately amount offered by selling security holders; if offering price cannot be stated, explain method of determination or cross-reference where described in prospectus and highlight cross-reference; examples of commission legend text are provided; underwriting descriptions may use clear concise descriptions including examples (e.g., 'best efforts'); requirement to limit outside cover page to one page; for asset-backed securities see Item 1102 of Regulation AB. The ‘Subject to Completion’ legend has required text and may be excluded in certain state-law-permitted offerings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Item 502 — Inside front and outside back cover pages of prospectus (Table of contents and dealer obligations)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a reasonably detailed table of contents on either the inside front or outside back cover page, showing page numbers for sections/subdivisions and specifically listing the risk factors section required by Item 105. Include the table of contents immediately following the cover page in any prospectus delivered electronically. On the outside back cover page, advise dealers of their prospectus delivery obligation including the expiration date and provide specified language where appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Table of contents must include a specific listing of the risk factors section. For dealer prospectus delivery obligation, use the provided sample language or other clear language; if the expiration date is unknown on filing, include it in the copy filed under 230.424(b). Dealer obligation need not be included if dealers are not required to deliver a prospectus under the cited statutes/regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Item 503 — Prospectus summary
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a brief summary of the information in the prospectus where the length or complexity makes a summary useful. The summary should be brief and need not contain all detailed information in the prospectus; summary business or financial information must be provided in plain English even if not captioned as a summary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The summary should not merely repeat prospectus text but provide a brief overview of the key aspects of the offering; registrants should carefully consider which aspects are most significant and highlight them in clear, plain language. Also include the complete mailing address and telephone number of principal executive offices either on the cover page or in the summary section.

rubrics_metrics.name: Item 504 — Use of proceeds
rubrics_metrics.description: State the principal purposes for which net proceeds from the offering are intended to be used and the approximate amount intended for each purpose. If the registrant has no current specific plan for the proceeds (or a significant portion), state that and discuss principal reasons for the offering.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Instructions: (1) If less than all securities may be sold and more than one use is listed, indicate order of priority and plans if substantially less than maximum proceeds obtained; (2) Detailed proposed expenditures need not be given — a brief outline suffices; consider discussion of liquidity and capital expenditures; (3) If other funds are necessary, state amounts and sources; (4) If proceeds will be used to discharge indebtedness, set forth interest rate and maturity; if indebtedness was incurred within one year, describe prior use of proceeds; (5) If proceeds used to acquire assets, describe and state cost and if from affiliates give names and pricing principle; (6) For financing acquisitions of businesses, disclose identity if known or nature of businesses to be sought, status of negotiations and brief description, unless disclosure would jeopardize acquisition — then more limited disclosure may be appropriate, and more detailed description required where Regulation S-X would require financial statements; (7) Registrant may reserve right to change use of proceeds provided contingencies and alternatives are discussed specifically.

rubrics_metrics.name: Item 505 — Determination of offering price
rubrics_metrics.description: If common equity is being registered and there is no established public trading market (or there is a material disparity between offering price and market price of outstanding shares), describe the various factors considered in determining the offering price. Similarly, for warrants, rights and convertible securities with no established market, describe factors considered in determining exercise or conversion price.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies to common equity and to warrants/rights/convertibles exercisable for common equity where no established market exists (see paragraph references). Provide a descriptive explanation of the factors considered in pricing or setting conversion/exercise price.

rubrics_metrics.name: Item 506 — Dilution
rubrics_metrics.description: Where common equity securities are being registered and there is substantial disparity between the public offering price and the effective cash cost to insiders (or registrant has losses in each of last three fiscal years and there is material dilution), include a comparison of the public contribution and the effective cash contribution of such persons. In such cases disclose: (a) net tangible book value per share before and after the distribution; (b) the amount of the increase in net tangible book value per share attributable to purchasers' cash payments; and (c) the amount of the immediate dilution from the public offering price absorbed by purchasers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requirement applies where insiders acquired shares at materially different prices or where the registrant has sustained losses and material dilution occurs; provide the specified numerical comparisons and calculations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Item 507 — Selling security holders
rubrics_metrics.description: If any securities are to be registered for the account of security holders, name each selling security holder, indicate the nature of any position, office, or other material relationship that the selling security holder has had within the past three years with the registrant or affiliates, and state the amount of securities of the class owned prior to the offering, the amount to be offered for the selling holder's account, and the amount and (if ≥1%) the percentage of the class to be owned by such selling security holder after the offering.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide identity, recent relationships, and precise pre- and post-offering ownership amounts and percentages; disclose positions/offices/material relationships in past three years.

rubrics_metrics.name: Item 508 — Plan of distribution
rubrics_metrics.description: If securities are to be offered through underwriters, name principal underwriters and state respective amounts underwritten; identify underwriters with material relationships to registrant and state nature of relationship; state nature of underwriters' obligation (firm commitment vs. agency/best efforts). Provide disclosures for new underwriters, other distribution plans, dividend/interest reinvestment plans, brokers/dealers arrangements, non-cash offerings, exchange offerings, underwriter compensation, underwriter representative board arrangements, indemnification of underwriters, dealers' compensation, finders, discretionary accounts, passive market making, and stabilization/other market-affecting transactions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Instructions and required details include: (a) Nature of underwriters' obligation need only indicate whether committed to take/pay for all securities or only to use best efforts; market-outs and conditions precedent need not be described except for agency/best efforts; (b) For new underwriters (organized/reactivated/first registered as broker-dealer within 3 years), disclose facts and sufficient details to appreciate experience and relationships; (c) For dividend/reinvestment plans state whether registrant or participant pays fees and anticipated cost to participants; (d) For broker/dealer selling efforts describe terms and volume limits, parties and termination conditions; (e) For non-cash offerings, state general purposes, basis, compensation and who bears expenses, and if part of acquisition/reorganization provide information similar to Item 504 Instruction 5; (f) If offered on an exchange, indicate the exchange and describe exchange-traded call option transactions; (g) Underwriter's compensation: provide a table showing nature and amount of discounts/commissions for each security and total, showing separate amounts paid by company and selling shareholders, and include all items FINRA considers underwriting compensation; (h) Table instructions: show cash commissions separately, disclose finder's fees, disclose offering expenses per Item 511, present over-allotment (greenshoe) info where applicable with maximum-minimum columns and describe key terms in narrative; (i) Describe any underwriter right to designate/nominat e board members and identity of any such director; (j) If underwriting agreement provides for indemnification of underwriters by registrant, furnish brief description of indemnification provisions; (k) Dealers' compensation: state discounts/commissions to be allowed/paid and other considerations; (l) Identify finders and material relationships; (m) Discretionary accounts: identify principal underwriters intending to sell to discretionary accounts and estimate amounts (pre-effective amendment if information not available at filing); (n) Passive market making: indicate intention and briefly describe; (o) Stabilization and other transactions: describe any intended transactions that stabilize/maintain/affect market price and explain effects and market/exchange; disclose that underwriter may discontinue at any time; if stabilizing began before effectiveness disclose amount bought, prices and period; if reoffering after rights/warrants offering disclose specified amounts and prices in supplement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Item 509 — Interests of named experts and counsel
rubrics_metrics.description: If any named expert (who prepared or certified part of the registration) or counsel named as giving an opinion was employed on a contingent basis, or had/is to receive in connection with the offering a substantial interest in the registrant (direct or indirect), or was connected with the registrant (promoter, managing underwriter, voting trustee, director, officer or employee), furnish a brief statement of the nature of such contingent basis, interest, or connection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Instruction 1: The interest of an expert (other than an accountant) or counsel will not be deemed substantial and need not be disclosed if the interest, including fair market value of all securities owned/received/to be received or subject to options/warrants/rights, does not exceed $50,000. 'Expert' or 'counsel' includes the firm/entity by which such person is employed and relevant nonclerical personnel. Instruction 2: Accountants providing reports should note Regulation S‑X §210.2‑01 for 'Qualification of Accountants' and disqualifying interests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Item 510 — Disclosure of Commission position on indemnification for Securities Act liabilities
rubrics_metrics.description: In addition to Item 702 disclosure, if the undertaking required by paragraph (h) of Item 512 is not required (because acceleration of effective date is not requested) and comparable waivers have not been obtained, include a brief description of indemnification provisions relating to directors, officers and controlling persons against liability arising under the Securities Act (including indemnification provisions in underwriting agreements). Include a statement in substantially the following form regarding the SEC's view that such indemnification may be against public policy and unenforceable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide the brief description plus the prescribed statement (text provided) informing that the SEC deems such indemnification against public policy as expressed in the Act and therefore unenforceable. Cross-reference Item 702 requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Item 511 — Other expenses of issuance and distribution
rubrics_metrics.description: Furnish a reasonably itemized statement of all expenses in connection with the issuance and distribution of the securities to be registered, other than underwriting discounts and commissions. If securities are offered for account of security holders, indicate portion of such expenses to be borne by such security holder.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Instruction: Where practicable itemize registration fees, federal/state taxes and fees, trustees' and transfer agents' fees, printing and engraving costs, legal/accounting/engineering fees separately. Include as separate item any premium paid for policies insuring or indemnifying directors/officers in connection with offering. Information may be given as subject to future contingencies; estimates identified as such are acceptable if amounts unknown.

rubrics_metrics.name: Item 512 — Undertakings (Rule 415 offering example)
rubrics_metrics.description: Include each of the undertakings applicable to the offering being registered. For securities registered pursuant to Rule 415 (shelf offerings), the registrant undertakes, during any period offers or sales are being made, to file a post-effective amendment to the registration statement: (i) to include any prospectus required by section 10(a)(3) of the Securities Act; and (ii) to reflect in the prospectus any facts or events arising after the effective date (or most recent post-effective amendment) which, individually or in the aggregate, represent a fundamental change in the information set forth in the registration statement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Item 512 contains a set of specified undertakings; where Rule 415 applies the registrant must file post-effective amendments to add required prospectuses and to update the prospectus to reflect fundamental changes arising after effectiveness. (Chunk ends mid-listing of additional undertakings.)
